args.understanding: The project is currently EMPTY (no parts, no logic — only the starter main.c), so despite the wording "add a button to the two LEDs", the two LEDs must be created too. Target behaviour: two LEDs (LED1 red on GPIO4, LED2 green on GPIO5) with a momentary push button on GPIO6 (internal pull-up, pressed = LOW). At startup LED1 = ON and LED2 = OFF. Every valid button press exchanges the two states: LED1 = old LED2 state, LED2 = old LED1 state (so press 1 → LED1 off / LED2 on, press 2 → back to LED1 on / LED2 off). One action per press (edge-triggered, no auto-repeat while held). Button polling every 10 ms with a short debounce; the press at t = 1000/2000 ms is thus acted upon within ~10–20 ms.

hardware.purpose: First indicator LED (red), state swapped on every button press
Current limiting for led1 (~6 mA at 3.3 V)
Second indicator LED (green), state swapped on every button press
Current limiting for led2 (~5 mA at 3.3 V)
Momentary push button that triggers the LED state swap

pin_plan.notes: Push-pull output; HIGH lights led1 (active-high through r1)
Push-pull output; HIGH lights led2 (active-high through r2)
gpiO_config with GPIO_PULLUP_ONLY; button to GND → pressed = level 0, released = level 1

wiring.purpose: GPIO4 drives led1 branch through r1
Series resistor into led1 anode
led1 cathode to ground
GPIO5 drives led2 branch through r2
Series resistor into led2 anode
led2 cathode to ground
GPIO6 senses the button; internal pull-up keeps it HIGH when open
Button other terminal to ground (pressed pulls GPIO6 LOW)

args.firmware_plan:
main/main.c (ESP-IDF v5.5, plain C, app_main entry):
1) Startup: set both GPIOs as outputs (gpio_config with GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT for GPIO_NUM_4 and GPIO_NUM_5, no pulls).
2) Set button pin GPIO_NUM_6 as GPIO_MODE_INPUT with GPIO_PULLUP_ONLY (polling, no interrupts — most robust in the simulator).
3) Initial lamp state: led1_state = 1, led2_state = 0; apply immediately with gpio_set_level(GPIO_NUM_4, led1_state); gpio_set_level(GPIO_NUM_5, led2_state); (first write lands ≈12–14 ms after reset). printf initial state line.
4) Main polling loop (no blocking waits, ends with vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10)) so the task watchdog is fed):
   - raw = gpio_get_level(GPIO_NUM_6);
   - Debounce/edge detection: keep prev_raw; a press event = (raw == 0 && prev_raw == 1). Because the trigger is the HIGH→LOW edge only, holding the button produces no repeats and the action fires once per press. (Optional 2-sample confirmation: require raw == 0 twice, i.e. ~20 ms stable — still ≪ the 200 ms stimulus press length.)
   - On a press event: uint8_t tmp = led1_state; led1_state = led2_state; led2_state = tmp; then gpio_set_level(GPIO_NUM_4, led1_state); gpio_set_level(GPIO_NUM_5, led2_state); and printf("SWAP: led1=%d led2=%d\n", led1_state, led2_state).
   - prev_raw = raw; vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10)).
5) Resulting timeline: states are always complementary starting (ON, OFF). Press at 1000 ms → (OFF, ON) applied ≈1010–1020 ms; release at 1200 ms → no change; press at 2000 ms → back to (ON, OFF) applied ≈2010–2020 ms; release at 2200 ms → no change. No long blocking loops, no PWM, no unsupported peripherals.

verification.name: Swap two LEDs on button press

risks: Project was empty, so the two LEDs requested by the user had to be created as well as the button.

If the firmware toggled both LEDs unconditionally instead of truly swapping the stored states, behaviour would be identical only while the states stay complementary — the implementation must swap the two state variables.
Polling period is 10 ms; keep all verification windows ≥ 30 ms away from expected edges (checks use 50–60 ms margins).
If the internal pull-up were omitted, a released button would float and could cause spurious swaps.
args.user_summary: 项目目前是空的，所以我先建好了两个 LED，再加上按钮。灯1（红）接 GPIO4（经 220 Ω 限流电阻到 GND），灯2（绿）接 GPIO5（经 220 Ω 到 GND），按钮一端接 GPIO6、另一端接 GND，固件里启用内部上拉（按下 = 低电平）。上电后初始状态为「灯1 亮 / 灯2 灭」；固件每 10 ms 轮询按钮，只在按下那一刻（高→低边沿）执行一次交换：把两个灯的状态变量对调并输出到引脚。因此按第 1 次 → 灯1 灭 / 灯2 亮，按第 2 次 → 恢复灯1 亮 / 灯2 灭，按住不放不会重复触发。验证场景在 1.0 s 与 2.0 s 各按一次（每次 200 ms 后松开），并逐段检查两次按压前后的亮灭状态以及整个过程中的翻转次数（每个灯恰好 2 次），全部用电路求解器测到的真实 LED 通断来判定。

args.summary:
Built the project from scratch: two LEDs + current-limiting resistors + a push button, plus ESP-IDF firmware that swaps the LEDs' states on each button press.

Circuit (matches the approved plan exactly):
- led1 (red, vf 1.9 V) — GPIO4 → r1 (220 Ω) → led1.A, led1.K → board.J3_GND4
- led2 (green, vf 2.1 V) — GPIO5 → r2 (220 Ω) → led2.A, led2.K → board.J3_GND5
- btn1 — GPIO6 → btn1.1, btn1.2 → board.J1_GND1 (internal pull-up, pressed = LOW)
No electrical warnings.

Firmware (main/main.c, app_main, plain C):
- GPIO4/GPIO5 configured as push-pull outputs (no pulls); GPIO6 as input with GPIO_PULLUP_ONLY, polling (no interrupts).
- Initial state applied immediately: led1_state = 1 (ON), led2_state = 0 (OFF); boot line over UART0 describes the program.
- Main loop every 10 ms: reads GPIO6, requires 2 consecutive LOW samples (~10–20 ms debounce) to confirm a press and latches it, so exactly one action occurs per press and holding produces no repeats; the latch is re-armed only after the pin returns HIGH.
- On each confirmed press the two state variables are genuinely swapped (tmp exchange) and both outputs re-driven, with "SWAP: led1=%d led2=%d" printed over UART.
- Loop always ends in vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10)) so the task watchdog is fed.

Expected timeline: press @1.0 s → LED1 OFF / LED2 ON (~1.01–1.02 s), release @1.2 s → no change, press @2.0 s → LED1 ON / LED2 OFF (~2.01–2.02 s), release @2.2 s → no change; exactly 2 toggles per LED.

Build: SUCCESS (ESP-IDF v5.5, riscv32-esp-elf), no diagnostics.
args.notes: The project was empty, so the two LEDs and their resistors had to be created in addition to the requested button. Debounce uses a latched press flag rather than a simple prev-sample edge test, guaranteeing one swap per press even with 10 ms polling. No PWM/peripheral features used — plain GPIO output/input only, which is fully simulated.

summary:
项目目前是空的，所以我先建好了两个 LED，再加上按钮。灯1（红）接 GPIO4（经 220 Ω 限流电阻到 GND），灯2（绿）接 GPIO5（经 220 Ω 到 GND），按钮一端接 GPIO6、另一端接 GND，固件里启用内部上拉（按下 = 低电平）。上电后初始状态为「灯1 亮 / 灯2 灭」；固件每 10 ms 轮询按钮，只在按下那一刻（高→低边沿）执行一次交换：把两个灯的状态变量对调并输出到引脚。因此按第 1 次 → 灯1 灭 / 灯2 亮，按第 2 次 → 恢复灯1 亮 / 灯2 灭，按住不放不会重复触发。验证场景在 1.0 s 与 2.0 s 各按一次（每次 200 ms 后松开），并逐段检查两次按压前后的亮灭状态以及整个过程中的翻转次数（每个灯恰好 2 次），全部用电路求解器测到的真实 LED 通断来判定。
